why:
Health signals are clean and the one anomaly is a thin, tail-only artifact rather than a regression. EVIDENCE: (1) Zero 5xx on both sides - 0/2384 canary, 0/7404 stable, 0.00% err on every endpoint and in all four 30s windows. (2) Canary matches or beats stable on central latency: overall p50 33ms vs 35ms, overall p95 95ms vs 95ms; per endpoint p50/p95 are /browse 22/27 vs 22/27, /search 47/60 vs 47/59, /checkout 79/102 vs 82/103. (3) No drift over time: canary p95 is 95, 95, 92, 95 across the four windows vs stable 96, 93, 94, 97 - flat, no warmup ramp and no late-window blowup. (4) The sole outlier is canary /search p99 652ms vs stable 61ms, which also accounts for the canary overall p99 of 172ms vs 104ms.

JUDGEMENT on that p99 spike: it is most likely outlier noise, not a code regression. First, /search p50 (47ms) and p95 (60ms) are identical to stable, so the latency distribution has not shifted - only a few extreme samples moved; a real regression in the search path would be expected to push p50 or p95 as well. Second, the signal is statistically thin: with 729 canary /search requests, p99 is set by roughly the 7 slowest requests. Third, the comparison is structurally unfair at the tail - canary p99 comes from a single pod, while stable p99 is pooled across 3 pods, which dilutes any individual pod's rare slow requests (GC pause, cold cache, one-off stall).

JUDGEMENT on risk: if the spike were real and persisted at 100% traffic, the blast radius is about 1% of /search requests at roughly 650ms - still sub-second, with zero errors or timeouts. That is mild degradation, not customer breakage, so the cost of a false rollback (blocking the release on single-pod p99 noise) outweighs it.

FOLLOW-UP: this promote is conditional on monitoring. During and after the ramp to 100%, watch /search p99 and max latency specifically; if p99 stays elevated with a larger sample, or p95 starts to move, roll back. Re-measuring /search tail latency with more canary pods or a longer run would have removed the single-pod sampling ambiguity before this call.
